packet.proposal: Set the alpine hut envelope to a compact 6.4 m x 9.2 m rectangular footprint with a 38-degree asymmetric gable, long slope facing north to shed prevailing snow load away from the entry.
inputs: Prevailing wind vector: 312 deg at 4.1 m/s (winter mean)
assumptions: Timber frame construction with 200 mm mineral wool cavity
No mechanical cooling; passive ventilation only
Entry approach is from the south-east trail
Foundation is pier-and-beam on exposed rock
packet.rationale: An asymmetric gable puts the longer, shallower slope on the windward north face so accumulated snow sheds away from the entry threshold rather than across it. The 38-degree pitch stays above the 30-degree minimum for reliable shedding at this snow load while keeping ridge height under the 6 m ridgeline visibility limit for the site. Compact proportions hold the surface-to-volume ratio near 0.72, which matters more than orientation at this altitude.
uncertainties: Snow load figure is a regional value, not a site-specific survey
Rock foundation depth unverified; pier spacing may need revision
Entry canopy not yet sized against drift accumulation

packet.proposal: Flag a conflict between the planner's 2.35 m eave height and the stated 58 m2 conditioned area: the resulting loft headroom falls below 1.9 m across 40 percent of the upper floor plate.
inputs: Loft floor assumed at 2.35 m above finished floor
assumptions: Loft is counted toward conditioned area
Collar ties sit at 60 percent of ridge height
Floor build-up consumes 180 mm below finished loft level
packet.rationale: Taking the planner's eave height and ridge angle as given, the loft plate intersects the roof plane where clear height drops to 1.62 m at the knee wall. Only about 60 percent of the plate clears the 1.9 m habitable minimum, so the usable conditioned area is closer to 51 m2 than the claimed 58.9 m2. Raising the eave by 450 mm resolves it without changing the pitch, at the cost of pushing ridge height to 5.8 m, still inside the 6 m limit.
uncertainties: Whether the loft is intended as habitable or storage-only
Collar tie position is assumed, not specified
Local code may define headroom measurement differently

packet.proposal: Read the envelope through a daylight lens: place a 2.1 m x 1.4 m south-facing glazed panel at the gable end and three 0.6 m clerestory strips along the north slope.
inputs: Latitude 46.5 N, winter solstice altitude 20.1 deg
assumptions: No external shading from adjacent terrain
packet.rationale: At this latitude the winter sun sits low enough that a tall south gable aperture delivers deep penetration when it is most wanted, while the north clerestories contribute diffuse light without the direct-gain penalty. Holding the window-wall ratio at 0.14 keeps the envelope heat loss within the passive target; pushing past 0.18 would require mechanical compensation the brief rules out.
uncertainties: Terrain shading not modeled; a ridge to the south-west may cut afternoon gain
sDA estimate is analytical, not a Radiance run
Clerestory detailing against snow drift is unresolved
